sentence: Although the weather was terrible we decided to go hiking
explanation: <Although> introduce un contraste: a pesar del mal tiempo, fueron de excursión.

sentence: Not only did she pass the exam but she also got the highest mark
hint: Not only + inversion, but also + clause
explanation: <Not only ... but also> requiere inversión en la primera cláusula.

sentence: Had I known about the delay I would have taken a different route
hint: Had + subject + past participle, would have + past participle
explanation: Condicional invertida de tercer tipo: <Had I known> = <If I had known>.

sentence: The project was completed on time despite the many challenges we faced
explanation: <Despite> va seguido de una frase nominal, no de una cláusula con verbo.

sentence: No sooner had we arrived than it started to rain heavily
hint: No sooner + had + subject + past participle + than
explanation: <No sooner ... than> requiere inversión y significa 'inmediatamente después'.

sentence: Whereas some people prefer city life others enjoy living in the countryside
explanation: <Whereas> introduce un contraste entre dos preferencias distintas.

sentence: The more you practise the better you will become at speaking English
hint: The more + clause, the better + clause
explanation: <The more ... the better> es una estructura comparativa correlativa.

sentence: She not only speaks French fluently but also has a good command of German
hint: Subject + not only + verb, but also + verb
explanation: <Not only ... but also> sin inversión cuando el sujeto va primero.

sentence: However hard she tried she could not solve the problem
explanation: <However hard> significa 'no importa cuán duro'.

sentence: Neither the manager nor the employees were aware of the changes
explanation: <Neither ... nor> conecta dos elementos negativos. El verbo concuerda con el sujeto más cercano.

sentence: Only after reading the report did he understand the full extent of the problem
explanation: <Only after> al principio de la oración requiere inversión: <did he understand>.

sentence: Much as I appreciate your help I think I can manage on my own
explanation: <Much as> significa 'aunque + mucho'; introduce una concesión.

sentence: Not until she apologised did he agree to speak to her again
explanation: <Not until> al inicio requiere inversión: <did he agree>. Significa 'solo cuando'.

sentence: So exhausted was she that she fell asleep on the sofa
hint: So + adjective + verb + subject, that clause
explanation: <So + adjetivo> al inicio para dar énfasis provoca inversión de sujeto y verbo.

sentence: You may use my office provided that you keep it tidy
explanation: <Provided that> equivale a 'if' con un matiz más formal: significa 'solo si'.

sentence: As long as you finish the report I don't mind when you start
hint: As long as + condition, main clause
explanation: <As long as> introduce una condición necesaria, similar a 'provided that'.

sentence: Even though he apologised she still refused to forgive him
explanation: <Even though> introduce un contraste más fuerte que <although>, seguido de una cláusula completa.

sentence: In spite of having little experience she got the job
hint: In spite of + gerund phrase, main clause
explanation: <In spite of> va seguido de un sustantivo o gerundio, nunca de una cláusula con verbo conjugado.

sentence: The new policy affects both employees and customers alike
explanation: <Both ... and> conecta dos elementos por igual, dando énfasis a que ambos están incluidos.

sentence: We can either postpone the meeting or hold it online instead
explanation: <Either ... or> presenta dos alternativas posibles entre las que elegir.
